_note: ONE table of the signing tools and actions, read by bin/chain-sign-wiring-test.sh (who signs provenance: REQ-CHAIN-001-AC1) and bin/chain-records-test.sh (every produced record type has a row: REQ-CHAIN-003-AC3), so the two judges cannot disagree about what a signer is. `regex` finds the call in comment-stripped text (a shell comment or YAML comment exempts nothing: it is removed first). `prov` says whether the call signs SLSA provenance: always | never | if:<regex tested on the command context> | unless:<regex> | fn:<resolver> (witness_run, actions_attest, cosign_attest, sign_blob: bin/chain-test-signers.py reads the whole command, or for a YAML step the whole step block, and FAILS CLOSED when the attestor list or the type cannot be read literally). `kind: step` means the context is the YAML step block, not one command. `pseudo` is the record type the records judge requires a row for when it has no finer resolver. Unknown signers fail closed: add the tool here, with a reason, before a workflow may use it. Modelled on: in-toto-witness docs/commands.md and options/run.go:64 (the attestations flag is -a/--attestations, a string slice, so -a slsa, -a=slsa, -a product,slsa and --attestations slsa are all the same request) and docs/attestors/slsa.md. Round 4: global flags may sit before the subcommand (witness --log-level debug run, cosign --verbose attest); -aslsa, -a=slsa, --attestations=slsa and a -c/--config file with no explicit -a all count as a provenance request (the config can list attestors); a cosign attest whose --type is not a literal non-provenance URI/short name is provenance (fail closed); testifysec/witness-run-action cannot be resolved statically so it counts as provenance. The engine is bin/chain-test-signers.py. Round 5: multi-line and folded commands, repeated --type, variable attestor lists, `-c` config files, `actions/attest` with `predicate-type:` on a later line, cosign sign-blob of a provenance blob, the python sigstore CLI, notation sign and in-toto-run are all in the table. Advisor decision, Oct 9: the table finds DIRECT signing calls only; which scripts a stage file may run is the allowlist grammar of bin/chain-test-signers.py (chain-scripts.json), not a search.
